what: Browser automation clicks and fills often did not reach the page. The builder then blamed slow app response and used many fixed waits and DOM eval clicks to move around.
why: Agent-browser tool problem. Refs went stale on re-render, text selectors failed, and clicks sent no events in several cases. Not an app latency issue.
workaround: Fixed waits (10 to 40 s), DOM eval clicks, direct location.hash changes, REST curl for data checks.

what: Creating a product through the browser form failed with 400 MISSING_REQUIRED_ATTRIBUTE, while the same create by REST succeeded.
why: Browser fill and keyboard input did not commit the numeric Price field (values were shown in the field but not in the React state). Evidence points to the tool, not the app.
workaround: Checked S03 with curl REST calls instead of the form.

what: kb_get returned 'not found' for paths that kb_search had just listed, so the builder could not read those docs.
why: Path resolution in the kb tool fails for some listed sections; index refresh was still running at the time.
workaround: Read search snippets, or grepped the catalog directly.

what: The kb read guard fired about 25 times with 'consecutive searches without consulting the knowledge base' while the builder read catalog files with bash and read.
why: Guard counts source reads as searches. It nagged on every bash call that touched the catalog.
workaround: Ignored; some turns then used kb_search.

what: Context-mode replaced long bash output with a search summary, so Maven and log output could not be read directly. The builder had to write output to files and read them.
why: Output summarising in ctx_search hid the lines the builder needed for the first Maven run.
workaround: Redirected output to /tmp/wsout files and read them with read.

what: kb_search results were fragmented and marked stale while the index was still refreshing.
why: Index refresh was running at the start of the session.
workaround: Re-ran searches later.

what: Paths under /tmp failed in the read tool (ENOENT) because the path resolves to /private/tmp on macOS.
why: Tool path handling for the macOS /tmp symlink.
workaround: Read the /private/tmp path or used bash cat.

what: judo.sh stop did not stop the foreground judo.sh start process or Karaf. The builder killed the leftover processes by PID.
why: Start was run under nohup and stop only tears down the Docker services and not the Karaf child.
workaround: pkill on judo.sh start and console.out, then restart.

what: The kb guard warned that three consecutive searches ran without a kb lookup, while the builder was reading generated files and running CLI commands.
why: Guard triggers on source reads and shell calls, not on a kb-first plan.

what: Browser tool: wait --text 'Hello' timed out even though the text was on the page, and wait @ref and wait --url also timed out on a loaded page.
why: Tool wait conditions do not match the rendered page reliably.
workaround: Took a fresh snapshot and clicked elements by ref instead of waiting.

what: Browser session repeatedly fell back to about:blank on its own. keyboard type wrote the quote characters literally, Tab did not move focus, and Meta+a and Control+a did not clear the field. Once the username lookup failed with 'Could not locate element'.
why: Browser tool issues: page state reset, literal key text, focus handling.
workaround: Reopened the URL, used the type command per field, logged the issue as a tool problem.

what: Orchestrator confirmed the browser tool delivers no click events to the page (a capture listener saw zero clicks for ref, text and raw mouse). set viewport lags and open sometimes leaves the tab on about:blank. The browser tool was dropped for checks and the round moved to Playwright E2E. Also covers the round 1 menu entry that would not open after login, which the builder first took for an app bug.
why: Tool-level fault in agent-browser, not the app or the catalog. Explains the round 1 menu click failure.
workaround: Round 2: checks rewritten as Playwright E2E tests; browser tool no longer used for checks.

what: judo fill --pages table added unrequested DataColumns (description and priceLabel) and changed dataFeature on them. The builder had to delete the description column by hand.
why: fill creates a column for every transfer object member, so the dry-run output had to be read before the real run.
workaround: Ran fill --dry-run first, then fill, then judo delete on the unwanted columns; the price column was removed on purpose.

what: Playwright chromium install hung for 10 minutes, then the downloaded Chromium binary was killed on launch (exit 137); every test failed with browserType.launch 'Unknown system error -88'.
why: Environment problem on this arm64 Mac with the playwright-managed Chromium build. Root cause not isolated.
workaround: Removed the cache and reinstalled; still failed. Wrote a local config (playwright.local.config.ts, not generated) that uses the installed Google Chrome channel.

what: Model CLI element names and paths were guessed repeatedly: query ui MenuItem, Access, PageDefinition title, GraphQL menuItems and _type fields, and FQNs with the id: prefix all failed with 'does not exist' or 'element not found' before the right names were found.
why: The CLI and GraphQL type and field names differ between query, create and graphql, and the catalog does not list the working names for the navigation and page elements.
workaround: Read the GraphQL schema with graphql queries, then used FQNs from the query output (e.g. webshop::Shop::Menu for the menu label, ProductInfo_Table label via webshop::ProductInfo::ProductInfo_Table).

what: judo move --dry-run printed the reordered element as 'changed ... description (in components)' rather than the element being moved, so the dry-run output was misread while reordering the form fields. The builder then ran discard --force to clear unsaved reorders.
why: The dry-run summary names the sibling that shifts, not the moved element, and the status output lists unsaved reorders by sibling.
workaround: Used move --json and graphql to confirm the child order, then discard --force and re-applied the move.

what: kb_get returned 'not found' for catalog paths that exist (agent-docs/frontend/README.md and best-practices/model/literal-derived-attribute.md). The builder read the files directly with read instead.
why: Path resolution in kb_get does not match the catalog for these entries, or the entries are indexed under other headings.
workaround: Used read on the catalog file.

what: CLI query of TwoWayRelationMember failed: asking for field partner without a sub-selection returns SubselectionRequired.
why: The query select syntax needs a nested selection for ref fields; builder did not know the syntax.
workaround: Builder queried fqn and primary only and used validate output instead.

what: ./judo.sh schema-upgrade failed with Non-readable POM for the schema directory; with -o schema_dir=application it ran for 900 seconds and timed out.
why: The schema-upgrade step expects a schema module directory and a running persistent DB; the default layout did not match this project and the run hung.
workaround: Killed the run and reset the database volumes instead of upgrading.

what: kb_get returned not found for section paths that kb_search had just returned (agent-docs/e2e-testing/model-screen-layout.md and agent-docs/frontend/esm-to-ui-mappings/widgets.md); builder then read the files by grep.
why: The kb_get path or heading lookup failed for paths that exist; the builder's TRACE also says platform-behavior-reference.md was not found by kb_get.
workaround: Read the files directly with awk and grep, and noted the miss in TRACE.md.

what: kb_get returned not found for an agent-docs/model/ui-authoring-guide.md section that kb_search had just returned.
why: Same kb_get lookup failure as earlier in the round; section heading lookup does not match.
workaround: Used grep and sed on the catalog file.

what: The Round 7 model script applied many CLI edits in one run with no check between steps; a partial run left unsaved edits, so the builder discarded them and reran the script.
why: CLI edits are applied one at a time, and a failing step does not roll back the earlier ones.
workaround: Ran discard --force, then reran the script from a clean model.

what: ctx_execute ran with /bin/sh and failed on bash process substitution syntax.
why: The shell used for the sandbox does not support process substitution.
workaround: Re-ran the command without process substitution.

what: Playwright could not install chromium on this machine (it hangs on extraction), so the local config uses the installed Chrome channel and no retries.
why: Environment problem with the browser download, not a JUDO issue.
workaround: playwright.local.config.ts sets channel chrome, workers 1, retries 0.

what: judo-cli.jar was missing from target/ after generate and build steps, so CLI calls failed with Unable to access jarfile; the builder had to run generate-root to restore it.
why: Cause not stated in the session; the target folder was gone after a build step.
workaround: Ran ./judo.sh generate-root before each CLI session that followed a generate.

what: The CLI query for DataColumn and DataFilter returned nothing until 'fill' had been run on the transfer object, so the builder first thought the table columns did not exist.
why: Column and filter elements are created by fill, not by create; the query output gives no hint of that.
workaround: Ran fill on the transfer object, then queried again.
proposed_target: judo-cli query output or judo-cli.md note on fill

what: postCallAccessNavigation cannot be cleared once set, and move --index had no effect on the position of the action group; move --after did reorder the menu entries.
why: CLI behaviour: unset is refused for this attribute and move with an index is ignored for these elements.
workaround: Left postCallAccessNavigation set (the clear attempt was refused, session:L2481); used move --after for menu order, since move --index had no effect.
proposed_target: judo-cli update and move (unset of postCallAccessNavigation, move --index)

what: judo-cli query --select on a reference field (target, access, hiddenBy, enabledBy, postCallAccessNavigation) fails with SubselectionRequired; a query written to a file once came back as blank whitespace.
why: CLI requires a sub-selection for reference fields; the error does not say which fields to select.
workaround: Re-ran the query with explicit sub-selections or printed to stdout.

what: create -t Access also creates a MenuItemAccess named Menu_n labelled with the target type name (AdminOrderInfo), so duplicate menu entries and not-unique errors followed; deleting an access referenced by a menu needs --cascade.
why: Side effects of Access creation are not documented for the CLI.
workaround: Deleted the duplicate access and menu, re-created one access, relabelled the menu.

what: Tool output wrapper replaced larger outputs with search stubs, so the builder re-ran commands; ctx_execute also rejected an unknown timeout argument.
why: Context-mode wrapper behaviour and tool argument schema.
workaround: Re-ran commands with output written to files; dropped the bad argument.
proposed_target: context-mode output stubs and ctx_execute argument schema

what: judo query rejected field names the builder guessed (cardinality on Access, claimType on ActorType, target without a subselection); the error lists the valid fields but guessing cost several calls.
why: CLI query has no field discovery beyond the error text; target needs a subselection.
workaround: Read the valid field list from the error and used the GraphQL-style subselection.

what: create -t MimeType with -n failed ('name' not defined for MimeTypeCreateInput), and the --brief 'valid' output printed Java object strings (MimeTypeImpl@hash) instead of names.
why: CLI create for MimeType takes no name; the list of valid values is not rendered.
workaround: Created the MimeType with --ns only and kept the default name.

what: judo.sh generate clean-deletes the target folder, which removes target/judo-cli.jar, so the model CLI fails with 'Unable to access jarfile' until generate-root is run again.
why: generate runs a maven clean that also removes the CLI jar in target/.
workaround: Ran ./judo.sh generate-root to restore the jar before using the CLI.

what: Table operation names are not the short names the builder used (exportOrders vs exportOrdersTableOperation::exportOrders), and ui query has no TableOperation type, so updates failed with 'element not found'.
why: Operation element naming of table actions is not obvious from the CLI output.
workaround: Listed the table operations with query esm TableOperation and used the full names.

what: validate --strict reported errors after a delete with --no-check, but the same command still ran save, so an invalid model was written to disk.
why: save does not stop when validation fails in the same command chain; the builder chained them.
workaround: Re-ran delete --cascade and validation until clean.

what: Context tool stub replaced 10 large shell outputs with a 'searches the whole output' message, so the builder had to re-run the command or read a file.
why: Output size threshold of the sandbox tool.
workaround: Re-ran with Read on a temp file.

what: kb_get returned 'not found' for a catalog path given without the catalog prefix, and a section named 'Table of Contents' returned only the TOC.
why: Path root and section handling in kb_get.
workaround: Used the full path or Read on the file.

what: The CLI rejects hiddenBy and enabledBy on a TableOperation ('not defined for input object type TableOperationUpdateInput'), although tables-navigation.md lists both properties for ui:TableOperation.
why: The CLI input type does not match the documented property list.
workaround: Per-row hiding moved to a separate page (see decision on F49).

what: judo-cli query esm with --where fqn=... returns nothing, and --select dataType{name} or dataType.name is rejected (scalar fields only), so the builder decompiled and grepped generated code to learn names.
why: CLI query selection rules are not what the builder expected; the catalog page on the CLI was not consulted for query syntax first.
workaround: Used name filters and grep over generated sources.

what: fill creates a menu item for every new access, labelled with the type name (ReturnableItemInfo, ReturnInfo, WishlistInfo). A hand-made MenuItemAccess with a duplicate name fails validation silently or with NamedElementIsUniqueInItsContainer, and move --index did not change the drawer order.
why: Generator creates menu items from access names; CLI menu commands do not change generated order.
workaround: Deleted the extra menu item, relabelled the others, and used the documented menu customizer for order.

what: kb_get on agent-docs/frontend/advanced-patterns.md returned 'not found', although kb_search had returned that same path.
why: Path mismatch between kb_search hit paths and kb_get lookup (unverified).
workaround: Read the file with grep and ctx_execute instead.

what: judo CLI query rejects several field selections: Access target needs a subselection, target{fqn} is not a field, TransferObjectType attributes{...} is not a field, binding needs a subselection, Operation isStatic and ActorType principal{fqn} are not fields.
why: The CLI query schema is not documented in the catalog in a form the builder could use; each guess cost a round trip.
workaround: Builder listed names with grep over fq() output and read the valid-field list printed in each error.
proposed_target: judo CLI query esm (field names and subselection rules)

what: judo query ui MenuItemAccess failed because MenuItemAccess is an esm type, not a ui type; the builder had to fall back to query esm for menu items.
why: Type names for query ui and query esm differ and the CLI error lists valid types without saying which lane holds menus.
workaround: Used query esm MenuItemAccess for the menu list.
proposed_target: judo CLI query ui (type lookup for menu items)

what: Browser snapshot selectors failed on text and role names (Products not found by text or by role name) during admin exploration.
why: Selector and snapshot mismatch in the agent browser tool; not verified further.
workaround: Used snapshot refs and waits instead.

what: Context-mode replaced large bash output with a ctx_search pointer, so the builder had to re-read files or re-run commands to see results.
why: Output above the size limit is indexed and returned as a search pointer instead of raw text.
workaround: Builder switched to the Read tool with offset and limit for the files it needed.

what: judo-cli query --select rejects many fields with unhelpful messages: binding and dataType need a subselection that the tool then rejects; readOnly, cardinality, isRowAction and AttributeMember do not exist. Builder needed several calls to find the valid fields.
why: Field names and subselection rules are not discoverable from the CLI help or the catalog.
workaround: Used the valid-field list printed in the error message and grep over JSON output.

what: judo-cli query with --where fqn~= returned nothing, with no error, so the builder's helper showed empty lists for DataMember searches.
why: Operator not supported by the CLI filter or failing silently.
workaround: Builder fell back to listing all DataMembers and grepping by prefix.

what: update --add feature failed for actions containers that do not exist yet ('Container not found', 'element not found'); fill reported 'unchanged'; a row action on a relation table was refused ('refund is not a feature ... placeable here').
why: CLI order of creating the actions group and row actions is not documented; error text does not say what to run first.
workaround: Used the generated refund table operation that already exists on the lines table; the test then opens the action group menu to click it.

what: judo-cli generate printed the line 'ERROR DATABASE HAVE TO BE UPDATED!' and then BUILD SUCCESS, so the level of the message is misleading.
why: Log level of the migration check does not match its meaning.
workaround: Read the message as informational and continued with the migration route.

what: New menu entries were labelled with the transfer object name (SellerInfo, SubOrderInfo, WalletInfo, AdminSellerInfo) until translated.
why: Menu label defaults to the transfer object name when a feature is added through the CLI.
workaround: Hungarian translations added for the new labels; the English menu text stayed as the object name at the time of this chunk.

what: kb_get returned not found for a section of agent-docs/backend/interceptors.md. The section heading was guessed; the file exists with H1 'Operation Call Interceptors Guide', and the miss does not list the valid section names.
why: Heading guessed from a bracketed kb_search hit; the not-found reply gives no list of sections.
workaround: Builder read the file with grep for headings and then the Read tool.

what: kb_get returned not found for agent-docs/e2e-testing/troubleshooting.md with section 'Speed Up Tests', although the catalog file has that heading at line 430.
why: Possible stale kb index or path mismatch; not confirmed.
workaround: Builder moved on without the section.

what: judo query on StringType with --select textWidget fails ('not a field'); textWidget lives on DataField, and the error lists valid fields without saying which type owns the attribute.
why: Attribute is on DataField, not on the data type; the CLI does not point to the owning type.
workaround: Queried DataField instead.
proposed_target: judo-cli query error message (owning type hint)

what: A batch of 178 judo update attribute changes produced 20 errors: 'element not found' for view fields that do not exist (email, ratingLabel, soldBy, remainingCreditLabel) and textWidget refused on a unit field. No listing of which attributes each view has.
why: Builder guessed the view attribute names from the TO fields; the CLI gives no per-view attribute list.
workaround: Accepted the 158 ok changes and skipped the 20 bad ones.

what: Standalone Playwright scripts with 'import playwright' failed (module not found, browser not installed); probes had to run through the project's 'npx playwright test' runner.
why: Script environment not set up for plain node use of the e2e dependency.
workaround: Wrote temporary spec files (zz-probe.spec.ts) and deleted them after each run.
